profile.product: RowRun (row.run), "your AI automation engineer" for sales and ops teams, built in Berlin by Uppacut UG. You describe a recurring business process in plain words (or drop the spreadsheet you use today); an AI agent writes it as versioned TypeScript code, runs it on sample data so you see every resulting row, then keeps it running on a schedule or trigger, processing each row as its own retryable job. Deterministic code for everything predictable, narrowly scoped AI agents only where judgement is needed, human approval steps, typed tables with SQL, a credential vault, and an MCP server so Claude, ChatGPT or Codex can build in the workspace. Servers in Germany.
profile.one_liner: Describe a recurring sales or ops process once in plain words, and RowRun turns it into reliable code that runs on every row, every week.

$2,000/yr; 2,000,000 credits, 250,000 rows per run, 10 GB; priority email support; unlimited members
$8,000/yr; 9,500,000 credits (about 16% off), 1,000,000 rows per run, 50 GB; extra credits $85/million; onboarding and a direct line to the founder
Done-with-you rollout, deployment in almost any environment, data isolation

targets: Head of RevOps, SalesOps or GTM engineering at B2B companies with 5 to 200 employees and a CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive)
Ops-minded or technical founders doing sales at a startup who build lists and research prospects without a GTM engineer
GTM engineers, automation freelancers and agencies running automations for several clients
Developers using Claude Code, Codex or Cursor who need a durable backend for recurring agent-built jobs
Finance operations teams matching invoices to purchase orders
Support operations teams triaging and escalating tickets
pains: Spending hours every week on repetitive, list-shaped work: copying HubSpot deals into a sheet, enriching leads, cleaning CRM records
Needing an automation engineer but not being able to hire one
Flowchart builders like Zapier, Make and n8n need someone to build and keep maintaining every node on a canvas
Chat agents like ChatGPT or Claude are great for one-off tasks but drift and give a slightly different result every run
Task-based and per-seat pricing gets expensive fast for bulk work on thousands of rows
Clay is powerful but starts at $185/month, too pricey for a small team
Not trusting an AI agent with the keys to the CRM, inbox and drive, and not being able to check what it did and why
Long automation runs that fail halfway and restart instead of retrying only the failed rows

use_cases.name: Find guests for a founder dinner

competitors.name: Clay
weak_spots: Entry price from $185/month (Launch), roughly nine times RowRun's $20 Starter
Focused on GTM data; not built for finance, support or engineering processes
No bring-your-own-key AI at one credit per call and no EU hosting

competitors.name: n8n
weak_spots: Produces a JSON node graph that someone must understand and maintain on a canvas
No native row-level durable fan-out with per-row results; workflows restart rather than resume mid-run
Execution-based pricing (2,500 executions on the EUR 20 Starter) adds up for bulk list work

competitors.name: Zapier
weak_spots: Task-based billing gets expensive for bulk list work (750 tasks on the $19.99 Professional plan)
AI Agents are a separate paid add-on ($33.33 to $50/month for 1,500 activities)
Output is not reviewable code and there are no per-row parallel durable runs

competitors.name: Make
weak_spots: Credits charged per module action, so large lists burn credits quickly
Scenarios are a visual canvas someone has to build and maintain; output is not reviewable code
AI Agents only in open beta since Feb 2026 and pricing is not seat-free

competitors.name: Gumloop
weak_spots: Agent-first design: re-runs are not deterministic by default
From $37/month on credits plus an orchestration fee
Weaker per-row durable execution and security certifications vary by plan

competitors.name: Lindy
weak_spots: Priced per user (Plus $29.99 to $49.99, Pro $99.99, Max $199.99), so costs grow with the team
Repositioned toward an AI executive assistant rather than list-shaped ops work
Puts the agent at the centre instead of constraining it, so results are less predictable
